title: Unclassified assignment literal: benign near miss controls (project-policy) [legacy tier T3]
summary: 1 input holding near-miss values that resemble the format but break it (truncated, wrong separator, wrong prefix or too short).
rationale: Incomplete or malformed values are not issued credentials. They test whether the format's structure, and not only its look, is what identifies a credential.

expectation.rationale: Relabelled by docs/decisions/2026-09-29-relabel-provider-named-near-miss-controls-under-948.md: was must-not-flag/T2 on aws-secret-access-key (a malformed-by-construction near miss, expected silence); is policy/T3 on generic-token with the value after AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY= as the secret span, expected action warn. Random or secret-shaped material under the provider's own credential variable is a credential under the amended project policy (redact-secret#948, amendment of decision-redact-provider-named-credential-assignments, 2026-09-29): generic-token claims it at the generic floors (redact at 16 bytes and entropy 3.0, else warn). No aws-secret-access-key provider-format claim is made.

externalRefs.note: Legacy benchmark issue the suite slice was written for.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Imported as a draft from the legacy suite "Beta.12 evidence for the AWS IAM user secret access key (#528, #1012 slice a)" (beta8-1012a); not yet reviewed.
